answer: An agent economy resists sybils by pricing admission with a bonded stake slashed on proven duplication: before routing work or voting, each agent locks funds behind its identity, and the ledger flags shared devices, funding paths and behavior. When two accounts mirror each other, the protocol burns both stakes, so every extra puppet costs the attacker a full bond instead of a throwaway mailbox, forcing real capital at risk. An echo of fake peers becomes a hollow shell once each is paid for, leaving a narrow inlet honest peers inspect cheaply.
